solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Convincing evidence of a bad habit, possible killer

parts.note: smoking tobacco is the classic bad habit
a gun is a weapon that may kill

explanation.surface: A clue that seems to be about health warnings: a bad habit that may kill you.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface links smoking and killing as one idea, but the clue splits into a habit and a weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: incontrovertible proof of guilt, like a weapon still giving off fumes after firing.

clue.text: Medusa's head has a decorative ribbon

indicators.note: the phrase Medusa's head has, holds, the run of letters within it

explanation.surface: The Gorgon's snaky head is adorned with a ribbon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has' signals that the letters sit inside 'Medusa's head', spanning the apostrophe-S and the first letter of 'head'.
explanation.definitionFit: A band of cloth worn over the shoulder or round the waist as ornament is a synonym.

clue.text: Test for a listener to take in

indicators.note: to take in means to contain, so the phrase for a listener holds the letters

explanation.surface: An examination for someone who listens, a hearing test.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to take in' says the phrase 'for a listener' holds the letters, spanning 'for', 'a' and the start of 'listener'.
explanation.definitionFit: A spoken examination, as opposed to a written paper, is a kind of test.

clue.text: Well informed, as was …

definitions.meaning: kept up to date, fully briefed
the clue runs on into 4-down: the film star appeared in movies, so was literally on screen

explanation.surface: A screen star is said to be well briefed, the ellipsis joining two clues into one sentence.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis carries the sentence into the next clue: the Hollywood legend of 4-down was literally in the picture, appearing on screen.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom meaning fully aware of the situation, versus a film actor appearing in a movie.

clue.text: … Hollywood legend spotted in dress circle

parts.note: garb is clothing, dress
O is shaped like a circle

explanation.surface: A film star is seen sitting in the dress circle of a theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dress circle' looks like the theatre balcony, but it splits into two separate words. Greta Garbo was a Swedish-born Hollywood star.
explanation.definitionFit: Greta Garbo is an example of a legendary screen actress from Hollywood's golden age.

clue.text: A foreign note, possibly false

parts.note: un is French for a, a foreign word for it
a natural is a musical note neither sharp nor flat

explanation.surface: A note in a foreign language might be fake.
explanation.walkthrough: In music a natural is a note restored to normal pitch, so 'note, possibly' gives the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: affected or artificial behaviour is forced, not genuine.

clue.text: Pine wood with name inscribed

indicators.note: written into the wood, so the name letter goes inside it

parts.note: a log is a piece of wood

explanation.surface: A piece of pine timber with someone's name carved into it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pine' looks like the tree beside 'wood', but it is a verb meaning yearn.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym as verbs: to yearn or ache for something absent.

clue.text: Camping gas available here?

parts.note: a bottled-gas supplier for campers is suggested, but the gas is the one breathed by patients, inside a hospital tent

explanation.surface: Asking where campers can buy fuel for their stove.
explanation.walkthrough: Camping gas suggests stove fuel; the real tent is a hospital enclosure supplying the gas a patient breathes.
explanation.definitionFit: A medical canopy placed over a bed to give a patient an enriched air supply.

clue.text: Superior being … one of five

parts.note: Superior is a North American lake, one of a group of five

explanation.surface: Looks like a reference to a godlike being, one of a group of five.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Superior being' suggests a deity; capitalised, Superior is the largest of the five North American lakes on the US–Canada border.
explanation.definitionFit: The five big freshwater bodies are Superior, Michigan, Huron, Erie and Ontario.

clue.text: Straighten out with distressing consequences

indicators.note: straighten out suggests sorting, but here the letters are put out of order

explanation.surface: Putting something right turns out to have upsetting effects.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Straighten out' reads as one phrasal verb, but 'out' is the anagram signal working on 'Straighten'.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: devastating or deeply upsetting, causing great shock or grief.

clue.text: One pays cash, say, for farm building

indicators.note: say signals the word is spoken, a sound-alike

parts.note: a purchaser, one who pays

explanation.surface: Someone paying cash for a farm building.
explanation.walkthrough: A byre is a cowshed; it is pronounced like the word for a purchaser.
explanation.definitionFit: A byre is a cowshed, a barn housing cattle on a farm.

clue.text: Abandon one's country for Golding's novel setting

parts.note: to desert is to abandon
one is I, and 's is S
a land is a country

explanation.surface: An emigrant leaves home for the place a famous novel is set.
explanation.walkthrough: William Golding's Lord of the Flies is set on an uninhabited tropical island where schoolboys are stranded.
explanation.definitionFit: The marooned boys in Golding's novel are on an uninhabited tropical island.

clue.text: It's not cricket to hit here

definitions.text: It's not cricket to hit here

parts.words: It's not cricket to hit here
parts.note: a boxing blow beneath the waist is illegal, unfair, just as 'not cricket' means unsporting

explanation.surface: A remark on where a batsman or bowler should not strike the ball.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not cricket' is a British idiom for unfair; in boxing, striking under the waistline is a foul, hence the phrase for unfair tactics.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom from boxing for a foul blow, extended to any unfair remark or tactic.

clue.text: They contain two feet of copper hose

parts.note: a bobby is British slang for a police officer, a copper
hose is an old word for stockings or socks

explanation.surface: Suggests lengths of copper pipe or hosepipe measured in feet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'two feet of copper hose' looks like plumbing; 'copper' is the British slang word for a policeman, and 'feet' are the wearer's.
explanation.definitionFit: Ankle-length socks once worn by teenage girls hold a pair of feet between them.

clue.text: Sounds like a drama teacher's old vehicle

parts.note: the stage stands for drama, theatre
a coach is a teacher or trainer

explanation.surface: Someone describes a drama teacher's antique car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sounds like' introduces a pun rather than a homophone: a drama teacher could be called a stage coach, and the word is also a horse-drawn passenger carriage.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse-drawn carriage running a regular route was the long-distance transport of past centuries.

clue.text: Old-fashioned, more suitable tailor

parts.note: out of fashion, out
fitter means more fit, more suitable

explanation.surface: A dated but better choice of tailor.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: one who supplies or makes clothing, especially for a particular activity.

clue.text: Obedient dog cut down on food

indicators.note: the verb is shortened, losing its final letter

parts.note: to dog is to track, follow
table here means food, as in keeping a good table

explanation.surface: A dutiful dog has had its food rations cut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dog' is a verb, follow; 'cut down' docks the K from TRACK. 'Table' for food is as in 'keeps a good table'.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: easily managed and docile, willing to do as told.

clue.text: More like one of the crowd

definitions.meaning: a film actor hired for a non-speaking crowd scene

explanation.surface: Seems to compare something to a member of a crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'like' is just a link joining the two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: something additional, and a walk-on background actor in a film.

clue.text: Have children, for example, protected by British and French

indicators.note: guarded on both sides, so these letters sit within the others

parts.note: et is French for and

explanation.surface: Having a family, say, guarded by British and French forces.
explanation.definitionFit: Archaic biblical verb for fathering offspring, to procreate.

clue.text: Suddenly total a hundred? Extremely close

parts.note: all is the whole, total
a ton is slang for a hundred

indicators.note: the extreme letters, first and last, of the word close

explanation.surface: Like a cricket score or sum suddenly totalling a hundred, very nearly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extremely' takes the first and last letters of 'close', giving CE.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: abruptly, without warning, all in one moment.

clue.text: US trickery is deployed to expose suspect terrorist

indicators.note: deployed suggests troops spread out, here the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: American cunning used to unmask a terror suspect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is deployed' looks like the verb; 'is' is part of the fodder, with 'deployed' the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A person considered a danger to national safety, such as a suspected terrorist, is an example.

clue.text: He informs on No 10's correspondence

parts.note: a rat is an informer
the number 10 written in figures looks like the letters I and O

explanation.surface: An informer leaks the Prime Minister's letters, No 10 being Downing Street.
explanation.walkthrough: No 10 Downing Street is the British Prime Minister's residence, but here the figures 10 are read as the letters I O. 'Correspondence' means proportion.
explanation.definitionFit: Mathematical sense: a proportional relation between two quantities is a correspondence.

clue.text: Pass is required in eastern state

indicators.note: in places these letters inside the state abbreviation

parts.note: VA is the abbreviation for Virginia, an eastern US state

explanation.surface: A travel permit is needed to enter a country in the east.
explanation.definitionFit: A visa is an official permit stamped in a passport allowing entry to a country.

clue.text: Part of way to the altar, an inch, perhaps

indicators.note: only a portion of the church walkway, missing its first letter

parts.note: the bride walks up the aisle to the altar

explanation.surface: A bride covers part of the walk to the altar an inch at a time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Part of' drops the A from AISLE. An inch is a Scottish word for a small island, as in Inchcolm.
explanation.definitionFit: Inch is a Scottish and Irish word for a small island, so an islet is an example.

clue.text: Rabbit or bird

definitions.meaning: rabbit is British slang for talk, from Cockney rhyming slang rabbit and pork
a small songbird such as the stonechat

explanation.surface: Choosing between two creatures.
explanation.walkthrough: To rabbit (on) is British informal for talk at length, from rhyming slang 'rabbit and pork' = talk.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: informal talk, and a small songbird of the thrush family.

clue.text: We never read our own at the end!

definitions.text: We never read our own at the end!

parts.words: We never read our own at the end!
parts.note: death notices in a newspaper describe a life after it has ended, so the subject never sees theirs

explanation.surface: Suggests people never finish reading their own writing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at the end' sounds like the last page, but means at the end of one's life.
explanation.definitionFit: Newspaper death notices summarise a life, published only after the person has died.

clue.text: London district's heads of security overcome huge odds

indicators.note: heads are first letters of the four following words

explanation.surface: A London quarter's security chiefs beat long odds.
explanation.walkthrough: Soho is a central London district known for nightlife.
explanation.definitionFit: Soho is an area of London's West End, an example of a district.

clue.text: Doesn't care about being poor

indicators.note: about indicates the letters move around into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone indifferent to being poor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doesn't care about' reads as one phrase, but 'about' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: inferior, of mediocre quality.
